title: The effect of ChatGPT on students’ learning performance, learning perception, and higher-order thinking: insights from a meta-analysis
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the unsettled question of whether ChatGPT meaningfully improves student learning. The authors note that prior studies have reported mixed findings, with some showing benefits for learning performance, perception, and higher-order thinking, and others showing null or negative effects. To clarify the evidence base, they conducted a meta-analysis of experimental and quasi-experimental studies examining ChatGPT’s impact on student learning outcomes.

The intervention studied is the use of ChatGPT in educational settings, compared against control conditions without ChatGPT. The authors systematically searched multiple databases for English-language studies published from November 2022 to February 2025 and included 51 studies yielding 72 independent effect sizes. Across the included studies, ChatGPT was used in multiple instructional roles, including intelligent tutor, partner, and learning tool, and in different application areas such as assessment/feedback, tutoring, and personalized recommendation.

The population base spans primary, secondary, and college students, though the included studies are heavily concentrated in college settings; the moderator tables also indicate secondary and one primary study. Contexts included STEM courses, language learning and academic writing, and skills/competency development courses, implemented under learning models such as personalized learning, problem-based learning, project-based learning, contextual learning, and reflective learning. The paper is not a direct secondary-school writing-feedback comparator study; rather, it synthesizes a broad cross-section of ChatGPT education studies across grade levels and subjects.

The main conclusion is that ChatGPT has a large positive effect on learning performance (g = 0.867) and moderate positive effects on learning perception (g = 0.456) and higher-order thinking (g = 0.457). Moderator analyses suggest stronger effects on learning performance in skills/competencies courses, in problem-based learning, and in interventions lasting 4–8 weeks. For learning perception, duration was the only significant moderator, with stronger effects in studies lasting more than 8 weeks. For higher-order thinking, course type and ChatGPT’s instructional role moderated outcomes, with stronger effects in STEM-related courses and when ChatGPT functioned as an intelligent tutor.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed meta-analysis of 51 quasi-experimental and experimental studies with explicit inclusion criteria, effect-size synthesis, heterogeneity analysis, and publication-bias checks. However, it is not a direct secondary-school writing-feedback comparator study, so relevance to the user's retrieval target is limited despite high methodological strength.
impact_tier_rationale: Reported pooled effects are medium-to-large and positive, including learning performance g=0.867 and moderate effects for learning perception and higher-order thinking. These estimates suggest substantial overall impact of ChatGPT-based learning supports, though not specifically for grades 9-12 writing-quality comparator designs.

interventions.use_case: Meta-analysis of quasi-experimental and experimental studies evaluating ChatGPT as a learning support tool across K-12 and higher education, including roles such as intelligent tutor, intelligent partner, and learning tool for tutoring, assessment/feedback, and personalized recommendations.

finding.finding_summary: Across 51 studies (72 effect sizes), the meta-analysis found that ChatGPT produced a large positive effect on overall learning performance (g=0.867, 95% CI [0.683, 1.052]). Language learning and academic writing studies were one included course category, with subgroup effects for learning performance reported as positive (g=0.531), but this paper does not isolate secondary-school writing-quality outcomes or direct writing-feedback comparator effects.
finding.measure: Learning performance measured primarily through tests and exams; includes language learning and academic writing subgroup outcomes
finding.effect_size: g=0.867 overall; language learning/academic writing subgroup g=0.531

finding.finding_summary: ChatGPT had a moderately positive effect on learning perception across 19 independent effects (g=0.456, 95% CI [0.287, 0.625]). Duration significantly moderated effects, with interventions longer than 8 weeks showing larger benefits (g=1.054), but the paper aggregates diverse constructs under learning perception rather than isolating a single secondary-school writing context.
finding.measure: Learning perception assessed primarily through scales and questionnaires, including motivational and attitudinal dimensions

finding.finding_summary: The meta-analysis reported a moderate positive effect of ChatGPT on higher-order thinking (g=0.457, 95% CI [0.255, 0.650]) across 9 effect sizes. Moderator analysis suggested stronger effects in STEM-related courses and when ChatGPT functioned as an intelligent tutor (g=0.945), but the evidence base for this outcome was smaller than for learning performance.
finding.measure: Higher-order thinking measured primarily through scales and questionnaires, including constructs such as critical thinking and creative thinking
